text: Run {highlight}/providers{/highlight} to connect an AI provider and start coding
Run {highlight}/models{/highlight} to pick the model for this session
Run {highlight}/init{/highlight} to generate project rules ({highlight}AGENTS.md{/highlight}) from your codebase
Commit {highlight}AGENTS.md{/highlight} to Git so your whole team's agents follow the same rules
Run {highlight}/help{/highlight} to see every command and its shortcut
Press {key:command_list} to open the command palette and search any action
Run {highlight}/settings{/highlight} to see every Lunos setting grouped by area
Run {highlight}/status{/highlight} to see your MCP servers, language servers, formatters and plugins in one place
Run {highlight}/themes{/highlight} to change the colour theme; Catppuccin is the default
Run {highlight}/whatsnew{/highlight} to see what changed since your last version
Type {highlight}@{/highlight} and a file name to fuzzy-search and attach files to your prompt
Start a message with {highlight}!{/highlight} to run a shell command, e.g. {highlight}!git status{/highlight}
Press {key:input_newline} to add a new line without sending
Press {highlight}Esc{/highlight} twice to clear the prompt; {key:input_undo} brings it back
Press {highlight}↑{/highlight} on an empty prompt to bring back your previous prompts
Paste an image or screenshot straight into the prompt to show the agent what you mean
Press {key:input_paste} to paste images from your clipboard into the prompt
Drag and drop images or PDFs into the terminal to add them as context
Run {highlight}/editor{/highlight} to write a long prompt in your own {highlight}$EDITOR{/highlight}
Use {highlight}@agent-name{/highlight} in a prompt to hand part of the task to a specific subagent
Be specific: name the file, the function and the expected result for faster, cheaper turns
Ask the agent to write a plan first, then say "go": fewer surprises on big changes
Mention the test command in your prompt so the agent can verify its own change
Use {highlight}/review{/highlight} to review uncommitted changes, a branch or a pull request
Press {key:input_undo} to undo changes in your prompt
Run {highlight}/new{/highlight} to start a fresh session without closing Lunos
Run {highlight}/sessions{/highlight} to see every session on this computer, across all projects
Group sessions in {highlight}/sessions{/highlight}: move them into groups and collapse what you're not working on
In {highlight}/sessions{/highlight}, use stop all to stop every running session at once
In {highlight}/sessions{/highlight}, clear list archives finished sessions, and show archived brings them back
Run {highlight}/rename{/highlight} to give the current session a name you'll recognise later
Run {highlight}/undo{/highlight} to revert the last message and its file changes
Run {highlight}/redo{/highlight} to restore what you just undid
Run {highlight}/compact{/highlight} to summarise a long session before it hits the context limit
Run {highlight}/fork{/highlight} to branch a session and try a different approach without losing the first
Run {highlight}/share{/highlight} to share a session, and {highlight}/unshare{/highlight} to take it down again
Set {highlight}"share": "cloud"{/highlight} to share sessions only with your organisation's Lunos console
Run {highlight}lunos --continue{/highlight} to resume your last session from the terminal
Press {key:session_interrupt} twice to stop the agent mid-turn
Press {key:session_background} to send running subagents to the background and keep working
Run {highlight}lunos session stop --all{/highlight} to stop every session from a script
Run {highlight}lunos session archive --finished{/highlight} to tidy up old sessions from the terminal
Run {highlight}/resume{/highlight} to list, pin and continue sessions
Press {key:session_pin_toggle} in the session list to pin a session to the top
Press {key:session_quick_switch_1} to {key:session_quick_switch_9} to switch between pinned sessions
Run {highlight}/export{/highlight} to save the conversation as Markdown
Run {highlight}/timeline{/highlight} to jump to any message in the session
Press {key:session_parent} to go from a subagent's session back to its parent
Press {key:session_child_first} to open the first subagent session of a turn
Press {highlight}←{/highlight} on an empty prompt to open the Agent Monitor with every session on this computer
Run {highlight}/monitor{/highlight} to see which sessions are waiting for your answer
In the Agent Monitor, type {highlight}@2{/highlight} to send your prompt to session number 2
In the Agent Monitor, a prompt without a tag starts a brand-new session
In the Agent Monitor, press {key:monitor.approve} or {key:monitor.deny} to answer a waiting request
Tag several sessions with {highlight}@{/highlight} in the Agent Monitor to send the same prompt to all of them
In the Agent Monitor, a prompt to a running session is queued and sent when its turn ends
Sessions waiting for your answer always sit at the top of the Agent Monitor
Switch to the Plan agent to get suggestions without any file changes
Press {key:mode_cycle} to cycle between your primary agents
Press {key:permission_mode} to switch between Manual and Auto approval; each workflow keeps its own
Press {key:model_list} to pick a model for this workflow; Build and Dev-Cycle each remember theirs
Run {highlight}/agents{/highlight} to see every agent, what it does, and edit it with proper controls
Run {highlight}lunos agent create{/highlight} for a guided way to build a new agent
Run {highlight}lunos agent export{/highlight} to share an agent, with its MCP servers and skills, as a bundle
Run {highlight}lunos agent import{/highlight} to bring in an agent from a teammate; Claude Code agents work too
Add {highlight}.md{/highlight} files to {highlight}.opencode/agents/{/highlight} to define project-specific agents
Give each agent its own permissions for edit, bash and web access
Set an agent's {highlight}temperature{/highlight} from 0.0 (focused) to 1.0 (creative)
Limit an agent's {highlight}steps{/highlight} to cap how many tool calls it makes per request
Pick the subagent model in {highlight}/settings{/highlight} with the same model picker as the main agent
Run {highlight}lunos agent run <name> --schedule{/highlight} to run an agent unattended on a schedule
Set {highlight}"tools": {"bash": false}{/highlight} to turn off a tool for every agent
Set {highlight}"mcp_*": false{/highlight} under {highlight}tools{/highlight} to turn off every tool from one MCP server
Override the global tool settings in one agent's configuration
Models blocked by your residency policy are marked "blocked by policy" in the model picker
Press {key:model_filter_cycle} in the model picker to filter by Recommended, Large or Small
Press {key:model_cycle_recent} to switch between your recently used models
Set {highlight}model{/highlight} in your config to choose your default model
Set {highlight}small_model{/highlight} for quick background tasks like titles and summaries
Run {highlight}lunos auth list{/highlight} to see every provider you've connected
Bring your own key: connect any of 75+ providers with {highlight}/providers{/highlight}
Use a local model through Ollama or LM Studio to keep prompts on your machine
If your organisation locks a model, Lunos tells you which one and why
Press {key:variant_cycle} to switch reasoning effort without changing the model
Run {highlight}/memory{/highlight} to see what Lunos remembers, where each fact came from and how it's used
Turn on memory in {highlight}/settings memory{/highlight}: the setup wizard recommends an answer at each step
Pick where memory lives: this computer, fully local, Neo4j or PostgreSQL in Docker, or a team database
Keep memory on this computer: only the fact text goes to your model, to pull out names and links
Choose the fully local memory template to keep memory and its model on your computer
Run {highlight}lunos memory check{/highlight} to prove memory works end to end
Run {highlight}lunos memory status{/highlight} to see where memory is stored, its size and its health
Run {highlight}lunos memory stats --json{/highlight} for the numbers {highlight}/memory{/highlight} shows, ready for scripts
In {highlight}/memory{/highlight}, facts never recalled in 14 days are good candidates to clean up
Mark a fact outdated in {highlight}/memory{/highlight}: it's kept for history but no longer recalled
Run {highlight}lunos memory search <words>{/highlight} to search memory the way the agent does
Run {highlight}lunos memory export{/highlight} to back up memory, and {highlight}lunos memory import{/highlight} to restore it
Imported facts are labelled as imported, with where they came from
Set {highlight}memory.encryption{/highlight} to {highlight}os-keychain{/highlight} to encrypt the fact ledger with a key in your keychain
Run {highlight}lunos memory verify{/highlight} to check memory's integrity hashes
Set {highlight}memory.retention.days{/highlight} to let old facts expire on their own
Memory statistics are computed on your computer; nothing about them is sent anywhere
Run {highlight}lunos memory templates{/highlight} to list the ready-made memory setups
Run {highlight}/marketplace{/highlight} to browse plugins, skills, hooks and MCP servers
Run {highlight}/marketplace mcp{/highlight} to jump straight to MCP servers
Run {highlight}/marketplace <words>{/highlight} to search every kind of extension at once
Run {highlight}/marketplace installed{/highlight} to see what you've installed and what has updates
Use {highlight}Tab{/highlight} in the marketplace to move between its tabs: Plugins, Skills, Hooks, MCP and more
In the marketplace, a hook's row shows the command it runs, so you can check it before installing
In the marketplace's MCP tab, each server shows whether your policy allows it
Every marketplace install shows a preview first; nothing changes until you confirm
Run {highlight}lunos marketplace add <owner/repo>{/highlight} to add another marketplace
Run {highlight}lunos plugin search <words>{/highlight} to find plugins from the terminal
Run {highlight}/plugins{/highlight} to turn installed plugins on or off
Your organisation can limit installs to its own allow-list with {highlight}marketplace_allow{/highlight}
The marketplace works offline from its cache and tells you how old the cache is
Write a plugin to send an OS notification when a session finishes
Write a plugin to stop Lunos from reading sensitive files
Add {highlight}.md{/highlight} files to {highlight}.opencode/commands/{/highlight} to create your own slash commands
Use {highlight}$ARGUMENTS{/highlight}, {highlight}$1{/highlight} and {highlight}$2{/highlight} in custom commands for dynamic input
Use backticks in a command file to inject shell output, e.g. {highlight}!`git status`{/highlight}
Find skills, reusable instructions the agent loads when a task needs them, in {highlight}/marketplace skills{/highlight}
Add {highlight}hooks{/highlight} to run your own scripts on agent events, for example before every Bash command
A hook that denies a tool call stops it: use hooks to enforce team rules
Create {highlight}.ts{/highlight} files in {highlight}.opencode/tools/{/highlight} to give the agent new tools
Write custom tools that call scripts in any language, such as Python or Go
Add {highlight}.ts{/highlight} files to {highlight}.opencode/plugins/{/highlight} to react to Lunos events
Connect MCP servers in the {highlight}mcp{/highlight} section of your config, local or remote
Run {highlight}/mcps{/highlight} to see which MCP servers are connected and which failed
MCP servers in a region your residency policy forbids are refused, with the reason
MCP prompts show up as slash commands marked {highlight}:mcp{/highlight}
Install MCP servers from {highlight}/marketplace mcp{/highlight} instead of editing config by hand
Run {highlight}/lsp{/highlight} to see every language server: running, failed (with the reason) or not started
LSP is on by default: the agent sees compiler errors after its edits and fixes them in the same turn
Language servers already on your machine are used first, before anything is downloaded
Set {highlight}"lsp": false{/highlight} to turn language servers off completely
Set {highlight}OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD=true{/highlight} to use only language servers you already have
Run {highlight}lunos lsp status --file <path>{/highlight} to start a file's language servers and see their state
Add a custom language server in the {highlight}lsp{/highlight} section of your config with its command and extensions
Formatters run after the agent's edits; configure them in the {highlight}formatter{/highlight} section
Set {highlight}"formatter": false{/highlight} to turn off the built-in formatters
Type {highlight}/claude <task>{/highlight} to hand a task to your own Claude Code, with approvals in Lunos
Type {highlight}/codex <task>{/highlight} to hand a task to Codex CLI from the Lunos prompt
Run {highlight}/claude{/highlight} or {highlight}/codex{/highlight} on its own to start a new session or continue a recent one
Run {highlight}lunos external list{/highlight} to check whether Claude Code and Codex are installed and signed in
In a Claude Code or Codex session, {highlight}exit{/highlight} closes that session and returns to Lunos; {highlight}/exit:lunos{/highlight} quits Lunos
In a Claude Code or Codex session, {highlight}/models{/highlight} lists that tool's own models
Use your Lunos commands in Claude Code and Codex sessions; on a name clash, add {highlight}:lunos{/highlight}
Claude Code and Codex sessions use their own accent colour, so you know where a prompt goes
Choose Claude Code's permission mode from a list in {highlight}/settings models{/highlight}, under External sessions
External tools default to manual approval: every edit and command asks in Lunos
Lunos doesn't write to your {highlight}~/.claude{/highlight} or {highlight}~/.codex{/highlight} configuration
Run {highlight}lunos external stop <session>{/highlight} to stop an external session from the terminal
In {highlight}/settings{/highlight}, press Enter on a section to open it, {highlight}←{/highlight} to go back and {highlight}Esc{/highlight} to close
Type in {highlight}/settings{/highlight} to find any setting by name
Run {highlight}/settings memory{/highlight} to jump straight to a section
Add {highlight}$schema{/highlight} to your config files to get autocomplete in your editor
Use {highlight}{env:VAR_NAME}{/highlight} in config to read secrets from environment variables
Use {highlight}{file:path}{/highlight} in config to include a file's contents
Use {highlight}instructions{/highlight} in config to load extra rules files for the agent
Put TUI settings in {highlight}tui.json{/highlight} and everything else in your main config
Run {highlight}lunos debug paths{/highlight} to see where Lunos keeps its config, data and cache
Override any keybind in {highlight}tui.json{/highlight} under {highlight}keybinds{/highlight}
Set a keybind to {highlight}none{/highlight} to turn it off completely
Turn on {highlight}scroll_acceleration{/highlight} in {highlight}tui.json{/highlight} for smoother scrolling
Settings your organisation locks show as managed and can't be changed in {highlight}/settings{/highlight}
Some settings need a restart: {highlight}/settings{/highlight} marks them with ↻
Run {highlight}lunos debug config{/highlight} to see the final config after every layer is merged
Set {highlight}"theme": "system"{/highlight} in {highlight}tui.json{/highlight} to match your terminal's colours
Create JSON theme files in {highlight}.opencode/themes/{/highlight} for your own colours
Give a custom theme dark and light variants, and it follows your terminal's mode
Use numeric xterm colour codes 0-255 in a custom theme's JSON
Press {key:messages_toggle_conceal} to show or hide code blocks in messages
Set {highlight}"tips": false{/highlight} in {highlight}tui.json{/highlight} to turn tips off
Set a {highlight}residency{/highlight} policy to keep model calls in the regions you allow
Memory setup shows what leaves your computer before you turn memory on
Set {highlight}audit.enabled{/highlight} to record model calls, tool runs and permission decisions
Memory recalls are audited as ids and counts only, never the text of your query
Permission {highlight}external_directory{/highlight} protects files outside your project
Permission {highlight}doom_loop{/highlight} stops the agent from repeating the same tool call forever
Use patterns like {highlight}"git *": "allow"{/highlight} under {highlight}permission.bash{/highlight} for fine-grained rules
Set {highlight}"rm -rf *": "deny"{/highlight} under {highlight}permission.bash{/highlight} to block destructive commands
Set {highlight}"git push": "ask"{/highlight} under {highlight}permission.bash{/highlight} to approve every push first
Use {highlight}LUNOS_OFFLINE=1{/highlight} to make sure Lunos makes no network calls of its own
Point Lunos at your own sign-in and console with {highlight}cloud.issuer{/highlight} and {highlight}cloud.endpoint{/highlight}
Your organisation can push one policy to every laptop with managed config
Allow once, allow always or reject, and tell the agent why you rejected so it can adjust
Run {highlight}lunos --sandbox{/highlight} so the agent works in a Docker container, not directly on your machine
With the sandbox, results come back as a branch you can review before merging
Sandbox network access follows your residency policy; change it with {highlight}sandbox.network{/highlight}
Use {highlight}sandbox.resources{/highlight} to cap the sandbox's CPUs and memory
Create a free Lunos account to start; no card needed
Run {highlight}/account{/highlight} to see your plan, your organisations and your role in each
Run {highlight}/login{/highlight} to sign in and {highlight}/logout{/highlight} to sign out
Accept organisation invitations in {highlight}/account{/highlight} or with {highlight}lunos org accept <org>{/highlight}
Invite teammates to an organisation you own with {highlight}lunos org invite <email>{/highlight}
Run {highlight}lunos org members{/highlight} to see who's in your organisation
Run {highlight}lunos org leave{/highlight} to leave an organisation you no longer work with
Your sign-in is kept in your OS keychain where there is one, else in a file only you can read
Delete your account any time from {highlight}/account{/highlight}
Run {highlight}lunos run --cloud{/highlight} to run a task on a Lunos Cloud worker; results come back as a branch
Lunos Cloud runs in its own EU data centre, operated by ITService EOOD in Bulgaria
Start cloud agents from GitHub, GitLab or Forgejo with triggers
Schedule cloud agents to run nightly: set it up in triggers
Run {highlight}lunos sync status{/highlight} to see whether this directory's sessions sync to your Lunos space
Session sync never uploads {highlight}.env{/highlight} files, keys or {highlight}auth.json{/highlight}
Add paths to {highlight}sync.exclude{/highlight} to keep them out of session sync
Use {highlight}lunos run "<task>"{/highlight} for non-interactive scripting
Use {highlight}lunos run -f file.ts{/highlight} to attach files from the command line
Use {highlight}lunos run --format json{/highlight} for machine-readable output in scripts
Run {highlight}lunos serve{/highlight} for headless API access to Lunos
Use {highlight}lunos run --attach <url>{/highlight} to connect to a Lunos server that's already running
Pipe text into Lunos: {highlight}git diff | lunos run "review this"{/highlight}
Run {highlight}lunos github install{/highlight} to set up the GitHub workflow for your repository
Comment {highlight}/lunos{/highlight} on a GitHub issue or pull request to have Lunos act on it
Comment {highlight}/lunos fix this{/highlight} on an issue to have Lunos open a pull request
In CI, Lunos never asks you to sign in; set {highlight}LUNOS_TOKEN{/highlight} to use cloud features
Run {highlight}/update{/highlight} to update Lunos without leaving the TUI
Run {highlight}lunos update{/highlight} to update Lunos and see what changed since your version
Run {highlight}lunos changelog --since <version>{/highlight} to see everything since a version you had
Set {highlight}"whats_new": false{/highlight} in {highlight}tui.json{/highlight} to skip the What's new panel
Press {key:leader} then a key to reach most commands; it's the leader key
Press {key:session_list} to list sessions
Press {key:session_new} to start a new session
Press {key:messages_first} and {key:messages_last} to jump to the start or end of a session
Press {key:messages_copy} to copy the last message
Press {key:sidebar_toggle} to show or hide the sidebar
Need more room: hide the right pane with {key:sidebar_toggle}, or click » at its top
Press {key:session_timeline} to jump to any point in the session
Press {key:terminal_suspend} to suspend Lunos and get your shell back; {highlight}fg{/highlight} returns
Press {key:input_clear} to clear the prompt
Press {key:theme_list} to switch themes
Press {key:messages_page_up} and {key:messages_page_down} to scroll through the conversation
Press {key:session_export} to export the session to your editor
Press {key:tips_next} to see another tip
Run {highlight}lunos debug lsp diagnostics <file>{/highlight} to see what a language server reports
Use {highlight}--print-logs{/highlight} to see detailed logs on stderr
If memory setup fails, Details shows the step, the reason and the log file
Use Copy diagnostics after a failed memory setup to include safe details in a bug report
If a Claude Code session can't start, {highlight}lunos external list{/highlight} tells you what's missing
Press {key:session_interrupt} twice to stop a long turn, then {highlight}/undo{/highlight} if you need to
If a plugin misbehaves, turn it off in {highlight}/plugins{/highlight}
Run {highlight}lunos debug info{/highlight} for version and platform details to paste into a bug report
Run {highlight}/tips{/highlight} to see every tip, search them and find the ones you haven't seen
